target: PleasantOther consensus (annotation col 3), HRF-convolved, placed at film onset
mask: posterior MNI gray matter, y < -60 mm, 43683 voxels
significance: withheld project-wide; descriptive effect sizes only
qc_note: five lowest-motion Tears of Steel runs, pre-registered by mriqc fd_mean BEFORE any decode; sub-S07 (the retracted June-7 PoC subject) ranks last 30/30 at fd_mean 0.554 and is excluded

positive_control_pooled.description: signal planted at each timescale, recovered via leave-one-subject-out; a valid estimator must recover the ~100s valence timescale
positive_control_pooled.verdict: PASS - recovers the planted signal at the valence timescale and uniformly across timescales; the estimator can detect signal

real_valence_pooled.description: real human PleasantOther valence, leave-one-subject-out, scored within each held-out subject
real_valence_pooled.verdict: NULL - the real decode (+0.089) sits BELOW its own circular-shift null (+0.127 +/- 0.042)

elevated_null_note: The Tears of Steel shift-null is elevated (+0.127) and wider (sd 0.042) than Payload's (+0.044, sd 0.013) because ToS is dialogue-light and visually intense: occipital BOLD carries strong stimulus-locked visual structure that even a brain-decoupled, film-autocorrelated target partly correlates with. A naive test against zero would have called the real +0.089 a positive hit; the circular-shift null catches it. This is the effect-sizes-not-p-values thesis reaching the brain arm from the neural side.
conclusion: Controlled null, replicating Payload. Occipital decoding of PleasantOther valence is not estimable above chance on Tears of Steel either: the positive control passes (+0.249 at the valence timescale) while the real decode (+0.089) sits below its own shift-null (+0.127 +/- 0.042). The two-film null (dialogue-dense Payload AND dialogue-light Tears of Steel), each with a passing positive control, removes the 'just a Payload thing' objection and demonstrates the naive-zero-test false positive.
